name: Atharva Poly-Plast Ltd
tagline: Rs ~130 Cr just-listed SME precision-injection-moulder for furniture, appliance and auto OEMs -- ROE ~35%, EBITDA margin ~20%, PAT up ~7x in two years off a tiny base -- but it is a small, customer-concentrated job-shop with no listed track record
business_overview: Atharva Poly-Plast (NSE: ATHARVA; recent SME IPO) makes customised plastic injection-moulded components and sub-assemblies (polypropylene, ABS, HDPE, engineering polymers) for OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers across furniture, home appliances and automotive. The pitch is a mix-shift toward premium/precision parts that lifted EBITDA margin from ~10% to ~19-20% over three years.
fundamentals_narrative: The three-year margin and PAT trajectory is impressive in percentage terms but the absolute base is tiny (~Rs 5 Cr PAT), and the numbers were achieved as a private company -- there is no listed history, no concall cadence, and micro-cap promoter-run disclosure. Custom injection moulding is a competitive job-shop business with high customer concentration and limited switching costs beyond tooling; the 'premium shift' is a plausible but small and unproven differentiator. Working-capital improvement (debtor days 52 -> 33) is a real positive.
technical_read: Not pulled -- freshly listed, no history.

verdict_headline: A real margin-improvement record on a tiny base, but a competitive job-shop model with no listed history -- 'neither', conviction Low
verdict_reasoning: No live-theme match -- 'engineering plastic / advanced plastic' appears in the priority-2 EV theme keywords, but this is commodity/technical injection moulding for furniture and appliances, not battery-adjacent advanced polymers; recency/lead pass.

four_box score 1.0 -> 'neither' (hard). tailwind weak, tam weak, moat no (job-shop moulding), valuation weak (~25x on a ~Rs 5 Cr PAT micro-cap). The small-cap live-inflection carve-out is not compelling here -- the improvement is a multi-year margin drift, not a sharp catalyst-driven recent quarter, and there is no listed history to judge durability.
